title: Symmetry-resolved fermionic correlations in iron-oxide ground spaces
authors: Federico Petrovich, Daniel Staros, Daniel N. Blaschke, Jian-Xin Zhu, M. Cerezo
abstract: Symmetries of quantum systems provide a natural way to organize the eigenspaces of many-body Hamiltonians. When degeneracies exist, however, they play a more subtle role as different sets of symmetry operators can resolve the same energy subspace into states with very different correlation properties. We study this interplay using a sequence of FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ models. For a Hubbard model of FeO, the ground space is 16-fold degenerate. Resolving it by local magnetizations gives a basis of Slater determinants, while total-spin quantum numbers select entangled and non-Gaussian states from the same ground manifold. Adding density-density Hund interactions breaks the independent spin rotations and reduces the ground space to a spin-reversal pair with maximal magnetization. These states are extremely close to Slater determinants in their natural occupations, yet have finite two-body cumulants and conserved-operator algebras whose orbit dimensions differ substantially from the Slater values. Fe$_2$O$_2$ provides a larger example in which spatial mode entanglement can be substantial while fermionic non-Gaussianity remains weak, with the conserved-operator structure again distinguishing the state from the corresponding Slater transformation class. Together, these examples show that symmetry resolution, mode entanglement, reduced-density-matrix correlations, and conserved-operator structure provide complementary information about interacting and degenerate electronic ground states.
summary: This work analyzes the complex ground states of iron-oxide Mott insulators by treating them as highly degenerate fermionic systems. The authors show that simply knowing the energy is insufficient; one must use advanced tools like conserved-operator algebras to distinguish between states that look similar but possess fundamentally different underlying quantum correlations. This provides a deeper diagnostic tool for correlated electron physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how different mathematical tools—symmetry resolution, entanglement measures, and conserved-operator algebras—provide complementary insights into the complex ground states of interacting fermionic systems.
main_result: The study demonstrates that even when multiple symmetry resolutions select states from the same energy manifold, these states can belong to different mathematical classes (different $	ext{GL}(n, \mathbb{C})$ orbits), indicating fundamentally different correlation structures.
method: The authors employ a combination of symmetry analysis (using commuting operators) and advanced algebraic techniques, specifically analyzing the dimension of the projective stabilizer algebra derived from one-body operators.
model_or_system: The research uses iron-oxide compounds ($	ext{FeO}$ and $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{O}_2$) modeled with Hubbard and Hubbard-Hund type Hamiltonians. The analysis focuses on the highly degenerate ground state manifolds of these strongly correlated materials.
key_observables: Mode entanglement, fermionic non-Gaussianity, dimension of the conserved-operator algebra ($\dim_{\mathbb{C}} p[\psi]$), and the $	ext{GL}(n, \mathbb{C})$ orbit dimension.
important_parameters: The system size is defined by the number of orbitals (e.g., 16 spatial orbitals for $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{O}_2$) and the electron filling (e.g., $N=12$ for $	ext{FeO}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on low-energy descriptions derived from DFT and assumes the applicability of symmetry-based block diagonalization techniques.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates that different symmetry operators select distinct states from a degenerate manifold, each characterized by unique values for mode entanglement, particle entanglement, and fermionic orbit dimension.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical models ($	ext{FeO}$, $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{O}_2$) and their symmetries, then introducing the formal machinery of conserved-operator algebras and $	ext{GL}(n, \mathbb{C})$ orbits, and finally applying this formalism to show discrepancies between different symmetry-resolved ground states.
why_interesting: The rigorous comparison of multiple correlation diagnostics (entanglement vs. algebraic structure) provides a powerful theoretical framework for distinguishing between different physical ground states in strongly correlated materials, which is highly relevant for understanding exotic quantum phases.

We characterize the resulting states from three perspectives: Mode entanglement probes correla- tions across a chosen partition of the fermionic modes, particle entanglement probes correlations beyond the SD description, and the dimension of the fermionic orbit characterizes the state under invertible one-particle transformations.
